Can the energy transition become the largest development investment opportunity of this decade?

We are entering a new phase of the global energy transition. The question is no longer whether it is happening, but whether our systems, our finance, and our institutions are moving fast enough to keep up with development realities. 

Energy is now at the centre of economic resilience and national security, making diversification of clean energy mixes a key opportunity to strengthen resilience in the context of rising geopolitical tensions. In 2024, investment in clean energy technologies reached USD 2.4 trillion. 
Demand for critical minerals could triple by 2030. Electricity demand is expected to grow more than 50 percent faster in the next decade than in the previous one, driven by electrification, cooling, and the rapid expansion of digital infrastructure—
But development realities are moving even faster. Regions where demand is growing fastest still receive a fraction of global investment.

This is exactly why, as @UN energy  partners, we bring together policy, finance, technology, and development efforts across the UN system and beyond, to move from fragmented actions to a coordinated, system-wide response—linking energy access, clean cooking, and just transition pathways.

UN-Energy connects expertise across energy, health, food, education, industry, finance, and digital to deliver at scale, responding to this new phase of the energy transition that requires integrated, interconnected solutions.

This week, I will be in Geneva for the #SDG7 Expert Group Meeting, convened by @UN DESA and hosted by UNECE - United Nations Economic Commission for Europe . The discussions will help shape the policy conversations leading into the HLPF and identify practical ways to accelerate progress on energy access and energy transitions, including clean cooking and resilient, diversified energy systems.

Looking forward to engaging with colleagues and partners in Geneva on how we can deliver a final push toward SDG7.
